title: Lacquer finish report
description: The finish report: the output of the grader (@lacquer/grade) and of the lacquer_grade tool. One report per subject: a component's registered implementation, or a screen. Every finding cites a rule id from dist/rules.json; scores follow grading/rubric.yaml. A subject is finished when its report has zero MUST findings.

component.description: The catalog id the subject implements, when the report grades one entry against its own contract.

renderer.description: The spec's implementation renderer: html, react.

file.description: Repo-relative path of the implementation the grader opened or imported.

package.description: The registry item or package that ships the implementation.

hash.description: Content hash of the subject's source so reports can be compared across runs.

detected.description: Catalog components the grader believes are present.

states.description: State coverage: every state the spec names, with whether the subject demonstrated it and whether it passed the state rules. The coverage grid on the report page.

status.description: pass: driven and clean. fail: driven and at least one finding names it. missing: the spec requires it and the subject does not demonstrate it. skipped: optional and not demonstrated, or not drivable for this subject (reason says why).

how.description: How the grader reached it: an attribute (`aria-busy=true`), an input (`hover`), a machine status, or a fixture name.

findings.description: Finding ids that name this state.

rules.description: Every rule the grader considered for this subject, with its verdict. A rule the grader cannot execute yet is `skipped` with the reason, never left out.

reason.description: For skipped: why the grader could not run it against this subject.

findings.description: How many findings cite the rule.

capped.description: True when a MUST in a gate dimension (rubric.yaml gate.cap_at_c_if_must_in: structure, states, accessibility) capped the letter.

dimensions.description: Only the dimensions in which at least one rule ran.

component.description: Catalog id, or 'screen' for universal findings.

state.description: The state the finding was observed in, when it was.

message.description: The rule statement, made specific to this instance.

reference.description: Path to the catalog's reference implementation or example that does it right.

summary.description: Two or three sentences for a human: worst thing first, then what passes.
